chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Remember Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, over the food, and do not be heedless/noisy, for it is a bounty from the bounties of Allah and a sustenance from His sustenance. It is obligatory upon you regarding it to thank Him, remember Him, and praise Him.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)
key_terms.تَلْغَطُوا: To be heedless or make noise/distraction

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette and obligation regarding remembrance of God during meals?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni’s al-Kafi, underscores the theological weight of daily sustenance by linking the physical act of eating to obligatory gratitude (shukr). It reflects the Shia emphasis on transforming mundane routines into acts of worship, where mindfulness prevents spiritual heedlessness (ghaflah) and acknowledges Allah’s provision as a trust requiring conscious acknowledgment.
